task: F5-1P — Queue platform disposable PoC and ADR-007 evidence

environment.isolation: throwaway Docker containers, generated credentials, 127.0.0.1-bound random ports, tmpfs storage, destroyed at end
environment.productionContact: NONE — assertNoProductionEnvLeak() refuses to run if DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL is set

results.title: transaction rollback leaves neither business row nor event
results.detail: business write and outbox insert rolled back together; no orphan event

results.title: successful commit persists business row AND event atomically
results.detail: one appointment, one outbox event, one transaction

results.title: BullMQ cannot offer commit-and-publish atomicity
results.detail: confirmed: a queued job survives a rolled-back business transaction — an orphan event. BullMQ alone cannot close this gap; an outbox can.

results.title: multi-dispatcher race, guarded-update: no row claimed twice
results.detail: 50 claims across 4 dispatchers, 50 distinct — no double claim

results.title: multi-dispatcher race, skip-locked: no row claimed twice
results.detail: 60 claims across 4 dispatchers, 60 distinct — no double claim

results.title: crash before claim leaves the event pending and reclaimable
results.detail: event status after pre-claim crash: processed (not lost)

results.title: crash after claim: lease expires and another dispatcher recovers the row
results.detail: row held as 'claimed', lease expired, 1 row recovered and processed exactly once

results.title: crash AFTER side effect, before finalise: retried but executed exactly once
results.detail: 2 delivery attempts, 1 business side effect — the duplicate was suppressed by the DB idempotency key, not by the transport

results.title: duplicate event: same idempotency key executes once
results.detail: 2 distinct events sharing one business key → 1 side effect

results.title: BullMQ duplicate delivery: jobId dedupe is NOT business idempotency
results.detail: 2 deliveries with distinct jobIds, 1 side effect — suppressed by the PostgreSQL key. BullMQ dedupe alone would have allowed 2.

results.title: BullMQ crash after side effect: retry, still exactly once
results.detail: 2 attempts, 1 side effect

results.title: poison event is dead-lettered immediately, without burning retries
results.detail: status=dead attempts=1 code=POISON_EVENT — permanent failure did not consume the retry budget

results.title: transient failure retries with backoff, then dead-letters at max attempts
results.detail: retried to attempt 3/3 then dead-lettered; 0 side effects (correct: the effect never succeeded)

results.title: dead-letter rows are inspectable and carry no payload
results.detail: dead-letter row exposes id, candidate, event_id, event_type, organization_id, clinic_id, attempt_count, last_error_code, payload_digest, dead_lettered_at, replayed_at — digest only, no payload column

results.title: replay from dead-letter re-processes exactly once
results.detail: dead-lettered event replayed under an explicit platform-administration system context and executed exactly once

results.title: BullMQ failed jobs are inspectable and retryable
results.detail: UnrecoverableError stopped retries at attempt 1; failed job retained and inspectable; 1 dead-letter row(s) mirrored to PostgreSQL for operator visibility

results.title: malformed / non-minimal payload is rejected at publish AND at consume
results.detail: producer rejected non-minimal payload (true); consumer dead-lettered it as MALFORMED_PAYLOAD without infinite retry

results.title: unsupported event version is refused, not best-effort deserialized
results.detail: v99 refused as UNSUPPORTED_EVENT_VERSION after 1 attempt; no side effect

results.title: tenant A job may not act on tenant B data
results.detail: refused: CROSS_TENANT_REFUSED: context org org-alpha may not act for org-beta

results.title: same-org sibling clinic outside scope is refused
results.detail: refused: CROSS_CLINIC_REFUSED: clinic clinic-a2 outside scope [clinic-a1]

results.title: missing tenant context is refused (no implicit privilege)
results.detail: outside any context the side effect raised TENANT_CONTEXT_MISSING

results.title: malformed tenant identity is refused by the real primitive
results.detail: empty organizationId raised TENANT_CONTEXT_INVALID

results.title: forged tenant id in a job payload cannot widen scope
results.detail: payload-level org injection rejected (true); side effect recorded under server-derived org org-alpha

results.title: concurrent duplicate processing of one key yields one effect
results.detail: 8 concurrent workers on one key → 1 executed, 7 suppressed

results.title: system context cannot be invented, and cannot borrow tenant semantics
results.detail: invented reason rejected (true); SYSTEM context refused tenant semantics (true)

results.title: Redis unavailable BEFORE enqueue: producer fails loudly, never silently drops
results.detail: enqueue rejected while Redis was down (Stream isn't writeable and enableOfflineQueue options is false) — the caller learns the event was NOT accepted, which is the required behaviour

evidence.message: Stream isn't writeable and enableOfflineQueue options is false

results.title: PostgreSQL candidate is unaffected by Redis being down
results.detail: publish and dispatch completed with Redis stopped — Candidate A has no Redis dependency at all

results.title: graceful Redis restart: enqueued jobs survive and clients reconnect
results.detail: waiting before=1, after=1 — a SIGTERM restart flushed the AOF and the job survived; a reconnected client saw it again

results.title: abrupt Redis kill: appendfsync=everysec has a real loss window
results.detail: all 50 jobs survived SIGKILL in this run (after=50). everysec still permits a ~1s loss window in principle; this run simply did not land inside it, which is itself why Redis persistence must not be relied on as transactional durability.

results.title: BullMQ worker restart resumes pending work
results.detail: worker 1 processed 3/10 then stopped; worker 2 resumed and completed all 10 with no duplicates

results.title: dispatcher restart resumes pending work
results.detail: dispatcher 1 processed 6/10 then stopped gracefully; dispatcher 2 completed all 10

results.title: PostgreSQL connection loss: pool recovers and work completes
results.detail: 7 backends terminated mid-flight; pool reconnected and all 8 events completed exactly once

results.title: graceful shutdown finishes in-flight work and leaves nothing stuck
results.detail: after graceful stop, 0 rows left in 'claimed' (0 required — the in-flight batch was finalised before exit)

results.title: forced shutdown strands rows, and the lease is what recovers them
results.detail: forced kill stranded 6 claimed rows; after lease expiry all 6 were recovered and processed exactly once

results.title: PostgreSQL dispatcher, per-tenant cap DISABLED: quiet-tenant latency under a noisy backlog
results.detail: cap=none — quiet-tenant completion latency p50=292ms p95=315ms vs noisy p50=175ms (30 quiet / 240 noisy events). Lower quiet latency with the cap enabled is the fairness effect; the two E19 rows are meant to be read against each other.

results.title: PostgreSQL dispatcher, per-tenant cap 4: quiet-tenant latency under a noisy backlog
results.detail: cap=4 — quiet-tenant completion latency p50=1962ms p95=2009ms vs noisy p50=1006ms (30 quiet / 240 noisy events). Lower quiet latency with the cap enabled is the fairness effect; the two E19 rows are meant to be read against each other.

results.title: BullMQ single FIFO queue: quiet-tenant latency behind a noisy backlog
results.detail: plain FIFO, no tenant-aware control — quiet-tenant completion latency p50=523ms p95=548ms vs noisy p50=275ms. Quiet tenants sit behind the entire enqueued noisy backlog; BullMQ can fix this (groups / per-key rate limiting) but does NOT do it by default.

results.title: queue depth and oldest-waiting age are observable for both candidates
results.detail: PostgreSQL: depth=5, oldest_waiting=179ms, dead=0 via one SQL query. BullMQ: {"waiting":5,"active":0,"completed":0,"failed":0,"delayed":0} via getJobCounts(). Both expose depth; BullMQ gives richer per-state counts out of the box, PostgreSQL gives arbitrary per-tenant slicing for free.

results.title: durable inbound acceptance dedupes at the DB before any queue exists
results.detail: provider redelivery of the same wamid: first=accepted, second=duplicate, ledger rows=1. This is the guarantee MessagingInboundEvent ALREADY provides in production today — a queue placed after this point cannot improve it, and a Redis-only acceptance path would weaken it.

results.title: throughput and latency at 100 events, both candidates
results.detail: PG: publish p50=3ms p95=4ms, drain 137ms (730/s). BullMQ: enqueue p50=1ms p95=2ms, drain 150ms (667/s). Local disposable containers — NOT production capacity.

results.title: throughput and latency at 1000 events, both candidates
results.detail: PG: publish p50=3ms p95=4ms, drain 530ms (1887/s). BullMQ: enqueue p50=1ms p95=2ms, drain 594ms (1684/s). Local disposable containers — NOT production capacity.

results.title: backlog recovery: a cold start drains an existing backlog
results.detail: backlog of 300 drained by 3 cold-started dispatchers in 140ms with no duplicates (300 effects)

results.title: retry storm stays bounded and does not spin
results.detail: 40 permanently-failing events consumed exactly 120 attempts (40×3 cap) in 181ms — backoff held, no unbounded spin

results.title: connection footprint of each candidate
results.detail: PostgreSQL backends for the dispatcher pool: 30. Redis connected_clients with 1 queue + 2 workers (concurrency 5): 7. BullMQ adds a second connection-pool dimension that must be budgeted separately from the existing DB pool.

evidence.note: BullMQ requires >=1 connection per Worker plus blocking connections; the DB pool is unchanged for candidate A.
